genre_note:
288 notes across 34 sub-plans; 55,554 of 56,804 words assigned (97.8%). Per-doc coverage: doc_0055 96.2, doc_0081 99.4, doc_0094 99.3, doc_0122 94.1, doc_0123 93.7, doc_0165 99.3, doc_0185 95.3, doc_0192 98.9, doc_0213 98.2, doc_0383 94.8, doc_0387 94.3, doc_0389 99.4, doc_0428 97.1, doc_0435 95.1, doc_0499 91.1, doc_0517 94.5, doc_0533 99.1, doc_0545 98.9, doc_0550 97.4, doc_0587 99.1. Verified programmatically: no (doc, block) pair is assigned twice, every block is either assigned or listed in dropped, all note filenames unique, all sub-plans 4-15 notes.

SHAPE OF THE CLUSTER. This is not news reporting. Five of the twenty documents are large ranked/curated listicles (doc_0094 "best movies of 2023", 50 entries; doc_0213 "best games of 2023", 50 entries; doc_0165 Halloween countdown, 31 entries; doc_0428 Switch couch co-op, 36 entries; doc_0055 Tubi picks, 8 entries) plus doc_0185 (8 per-platform TV picks) and doc_0081 (19 announced DC projects). That is 202 of the 288 notes. Each list entry is a self-contained subject with its own director/developer, cast, premise and where-to-watch line, so each got its own note; merging entries by rank band would have produced notes retrieved for everything and answering nothing. Density was never the binding constraint (the largest note, the Diablo 4 Firewall build, is ~650 source words); topical coherence set every boundary.

BUILDING-BLOCK DISTRIBUTION AND WHAT IS ABSENT. concept 216, empirical_observation 34, model 11, argument 11, procedure 11, counter_argument 5, hypothesis 0, navigation 0. The concept skew is a genuine property of curated-recommendation entertainment coverage: the dominant question each block answers is "What is X?" (this film, this game, this show, this announced project), not "What happened?". empirical_observation is concentrated in the six actual news/feature pieces (doc_0499 event schedule, doc_0517 demonetization, doc_0533 patch notes, doc_0435/0545/0550 TwitchCon reporting, doc_0587 Elfman). procedure appears only where the source genuinely gives ordered steps: Diablo 4 skill-point orders and glyph-leveling orders, Monster Hunter Now quest steps and ticket farming, and the four editorial list-methodology notes. hypothesis: ZERO. No document in this cluster advances a testable prediction; the forward-looking material (doc_0081's undated slate, doc_0545's cost projections) is announcement or trend description, not conjecture, and I did not manufacture any. navigation: zero, as instructed.

SHARED ENTITY NOTES (six, each drawing blocks from two documents, never duplicating a pair): killers_of_the_flower_moon_film (doc_0094 top-50 entry + doc_0192's dedicated section); marvels_spider_man_2_game (doc_0213 entry + doc_0383 review); spider_man_across_the_spider_verse (doc_0094 entry + doc_0383's exposition of its "canon events"); skinamarink_kyle_edward_ball (doc_0094 entry + doc_0165's account of its polarizing reception, reached via the Heck short); super_mario_bros_wonder (doc_0213 entry + doc_0428 co-op blurb); diablo_4_season_2_vampiric_powers (the identical system explanation in doc_0122 and doc_0123). Where documents share an entity but not a subject I kept them separate and let the graph link them: doc_0213's Diablo 4 entry vs. doc_0122/0123 class builds vs. doc_0533 Season of Blood; doc_0213's Monster Hunter Now entry vs. doc_0499's Halloween event; doc_0213's Tears of the Kingdom entry vs. doc_0389's gender criticism.

BLOCKS I INSPECTED BEFORE DROPPING, AND KEPT. doc_0587 block 17 reads as a routine correction notice but actually restates the year of the Royal Albert Hall performance, a scope condition on the "return to live performance" claim; assigned. doc_0081 block 4 is an editor's note restricting the whole slate to Warner Bros. DC and excluding the Arrowverse; assigned to the reboot note. doc_0094 block 8 states the eligibility cutoff for the ranking; assigned to the methodology note. doc_0213 block 168 is an editor's note explaining that Midnight Suns shipped in 2022 and missed the previous cutoff; assigned. doc_0428 block 29 carries the parenthetical that Diablo 4 never came to Switch; assigned. doc_0383 block 13 is a spoiler warning that scopes the canon-events argument; assigned. doc_0499 block 32 credits a Reddit user for filling gaps in the quest table, which is a reliability caveat on that table; assigned. doc_0499 block 35, an image credit, is borderline and I assigned it rather than drop it.

WHAT I DROPPED. Only chrome: article titles (carried in note H1s), rank/section headers ("Top 50", "2024", "For two players", FAQ question headers, guide H2s), the boilerplate "Polygon's What to Watch / What to Play" newsletter blurb, the identical "Polygon is celebrating TwitchCon 2023 with a package of stories" promo appearing in doc_0435/0545/0550, doc_0213's twenty "Related <headline>" cross-promo links, "Looking for other Diablo 4 builds?" and "Looking for more guides?" footers, doc_0435's duplicated headline and share widget, doc_0517's "Polygon reached out and will update this story", doc_0055's "Let's get into it.", and doc_0383's "Polygon Recommends is our way of endorsing" badge explainer.

LOWEST-COVERAGE DOCUMENTS AND WHY. doc_0499 (91.1%), doc_0123 (93.7%) and doc_0122 (94.1%) are short how-to guides whose word count is unusually header-dense: doc_0122 alone has thirteen H2/H3 section headers over 1,601 words. Their dropped words are almost entirely those headers plus one cross-promo footer, not substance. doc_0387 (94.3%) is a Q&A whose six question headers become note titles. doc_0517 (94.5%) and doc_0383 (94.8%) lose the "we reached out" line and the Polygon Recommends badge respectively. No document in this cluster is mostly promotional.

Note on rank information: for the three ranked lists I deliberately assigned the numbered entry-title blocks (e.g. doc_0213 block 309 "1. The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom") rather than dropping them as headers, because the rank itself is substantive content that a multi-hop question could turn on.
